FR12 ruling (owner decision of 2026-10-16): a replaced file is always refused. confirm_verified(fd, sha256, identity, path) now compares st_dev and st_ino of lstat(path) with those of fstat on the verified descriptor at the check point; any difference, or a path that no longer exists, refuses with 'changed', independent of any clock. The ctime check stays as an extra signal (a write followed by an mtime reset); it is never the only signal. The same path identity rule already holds in the restore check of the native job (container/bench_native_job.py _still_verified). Consequence of the rule: a swap of the directory that holds the file now refuses as well (at the check point the path names another file), so the three directory-swap tests now expect the refusal, and each asserts that the swapped file never runs: the kernel test finds no marker of the swapped file; the worker test finds that the started process runs the interpreter of the verified peer (not /bin/sh of the swapped file) and no marker, and that the process is refused and reaped (FR12-A01); the inproc test finds that the loader saw only the verified bytes. The tick tests stay; the new tests cover the same refusal more strongly: a rename over with no clock wait, and a rename over with the ctime signal removed (the no-tick case made deterministic), for each route. The new unchanged-file tests pass (the kernel test also asserts the start from /proc/self/fd/N).
